speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin; this is called jaundice. To determine the cause, have you noticed your baby feeding well or passing stool normally? When did you first notice the yellow color appearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding-associated jaundice (early-onset). The patient is a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with increasing jaundice, normal weight gain (3066g to 3200g), and no mention of poor feeding or stool changes, which strongly suggests insufficient intake rather than pathologic causes like hemolysis or infection. No further tests or images are required; the plan is to increase breastfeeding frequency or supplement with expressed breast milk.
